newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police grill 20 suspected Moslem militants.
newsitem.headline: French police grill 20 suspected Moslem militants.

text.p: Police hunting for clues to the bombing of a Paris commuter train rounded up 20 suspected Moslem fundamentalists in pre-dawn raids in the Paris region and northern France on Thursday, a police official said.

Justice sources said the new police raid on Islamist circles, the third since the December 3 train attack, was part of investigators' hunt for leads in the bombing, which killed four commuters. It yielded little, a police source told Reuters.
All 23 people detained in the two earlier raids were released after questioning.

The latest raids also appeared linked to a shadowy gang, some of whose members converted to Moslem fundamentalism, which was blamed for robberies in northern France. Four members of the gang were killed in a shootout with police last year.

Police suspect Moslem guerrillas linked to Algeria carried out this month's Port Royal underground station attack, because the bombing closely resembled a wave of attacks that killed eight people last year, claimed by fundamentalists unhappy over France's support for the Algerian authorities.
Meanwhile, police confirmed that alert security guards at a central Paris store had stopped three men of suspected North African origin handling a gas canister with nails and bolts last weekend.
Gas canisters filled with explosives, nails and screws were used in this month's and most of last year's attacks.
The three men fled the clothing store in the busy Opera district. Police said the canister contained no explosives or detonator but bags of nails and screws were found nearby.
A police spokesman said detectives were not sure whether the incident was linked to terrorism.
Security measures have been drastically stepped up in the Paris underground railway network and department stores for fear of more attacks during the busy Christmas shopping period.
